verdict.rationale: Ramp documents its own event-driven automations that users configure: dynamic approval routing, auto top-up against a target balance with low-balance alerts, and a customizable human-in-the-loop policy that auto-approves routine agent spend. These are fixed, domain-specific automations rather than a general user-defined rules engine. Webhooks push events, but acting on them requires the user's own handler service, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: a documented general-purpose rule builder (arbitrary event → condition → action), native in-product actions on webhook events without external handlers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Dynamic approval routing with parallel workflows across finance, IT, legal, and security
Auto top-up from linked checking accounts with target balance automation and low balance alerts
Customizable human-in-the-loop policy — auto-approve the routine, hold what matters for a human.
